title: POC scoping: NyxAI - open models shortlist
summary: AE + SE from Redwood scoped a POC for NyxAI to evaluate open-model inference for multilingual, domain-specific question answering. Discussed success metrics (latency under 200ms for short queries, recall/accuracy thresholds on internal eval set), workload profile (mix of short queries and long-context summarization), model shortlist tradeoffs (Mistral, Llama-3 variants, Falcon, MPT), and POC timeline (2-4 week bench + 4 week pilot). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan, pricing for hosted vs dedicated, and SOC2/security pack; customer to provide 500 sample queries and an eval script.
header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recorded: yes
Redwood: Jordan Mills (AE), Priya Singh (SE)
NyxAI: Dr. Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Marcus Chen (Platform), Aisha Bello (Product), Tariq Al-Sayeed (Infra)
Files shared: NyxAI_sample_queries.csv (customer), Redwood_poc_playbook.pdf (link), benchmark_template.xlsx (link)
transcript:
[00:00:05] Jordan Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Lena here. Hi.
[00:00:15] Marcus Chen: Marcus, hey.
[00:00:17] Aisha Bello: Aisha—product.
[00:00:20] Jordan Mills: Awesome. Priya from our infra side is here, she'll drive the bench details. Priya?
[00:00:26] Priya Singh: Hey all, thanks. I'll mostly cover workload sizing and the benchmark plan.
[00:00:32] Jordan Mills: High level, NyxAI wants to test open models for qa and summarization over internal docs, multi-lingual in EN/ES/PT, and need a sense of latency/cost tradeoffs. Is that right, Lena?
[00:00:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Yeah that's right. We have a few constraints: PII redaction requirement, preference to avoid sending certain data to third-party hosted models if we can avoid it, and a SLO for web UI latencies — ideally sub 200ms for short QA, but we know that's tough.
[00:00:55] Jordan Mills: Great. Can we walk through success criteria? what does a successful POC look like for you?
[00:01:02] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Two things — accuracy on our eval set, target F1-like metric > 0.78 for extraction QA; and response time: 90th percentile under 400ms for typical short queries, pref under 200ms if possible. plus operational: can we run on dedicated infra or VPC? and SOC2 and KMS integration for keys.
[00:01:20] Marcus Chen: Also cost envelope — we're a startup but with enterprise customers, so we need clear per-1M token estimates and a path to dedicated capacity if the model looks promising.
[00:01:30] Jordan Mills: Makes sense. Priya, workload profile?
[00:01:33] Priya Singh: Based on their description, we'll treat this as hybrid: 70% short QA requests (10-60 tokens), 20% medium instructs (60-300 tokens), 10% long-context summarization (1k-3k tokens) for single-pass. Average concurrency estimate they gave is ~80 qps peak across global region, but for POC we scale a smaller replica that simulates ~20-30 qps sustained to start.
[00:01:55] Marcus Chen: The 80 qps is optimistic; our immediate production would be closer to 25 qps, so POC at 20-30 qps is fine. We can also provide a sample replay of queries.
[00:02:04] Jordan Mills: Cool. On models: we proposed an open-model shortlist to balance quality and cost — Priya will walk tradeoffs.
[00:02:10] Priya Singh: Shortlist: Mistral 7B Instruct, Llama-3 13B (quantized variants), Falcon 40B (if legal clears), MPT-30B, and a tuned OpenAssistant/Guanaco style 13B. Quick notes: Mistral 7B gives excellent latency/cost for many instruction tasks; Llama-3 13B (float16 or 4-bit) often hits a good quality point for QA; Falcon-40 tends to be better on some knowledge tasks but is heavier; MPT/Mistral scale differently; tuned Guanaco might work well for domain-specific prompts.
[00:02:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Are there big multilingual differences? Spanish/Portuguese are critical for us.
[00:02:49] Priya Singh: Right — Mistral and Llama-3 variants tend to do okay in Spanish; Falcon historically weaker on some languages but there are tuned checkpoints. We'll include a small multilingual eval in the benchmark, about 150 queries across EN/ES/PT.
[00:03:03] Aisha Bello: For domain adaptation, we plan to run a small fine-tune or LoRA later if base model quality is off. For the POC, we just need to see improvement over baseline (current open-source model) by >8-10% on our metrics.
[00:03:15] Jordan Mills: On the infra side — you'd prefer VPC/private deployment?
[00:03:18] Tariq Al-Sayeed: Yes, ideally VPC peering for Dedicated, but for bench we can do hosted with data obfuscated. We need KMS for key management, SSO (SAML) and audit logs.
[00:03:28] Priya Singh: We can support hosted inference for bench with strict retention settings and then run Dedicated (VPC) for pilot. Redwood supports KMS integration and RBAC; we'll share SOC2 docs and an architecture note.
[00:03:39] Marcus Chen: Any limitations on KV cache or long-context? our summarization pieces will sometimes need 3k token context.
[00:03:45] Priya Singh: Our runtime supports up to 8k in most configs; quantization profiles can impact memory for KV cache slightly. For 3k contexts we'll configure batch sizes accordingly, and we can show memory/perf numbers in the bench. There might be slight increase in latency for long context but batching and prefix caching helps.
[00:04:01] Jordan Mills: Benchmarks — Priya, what will you measure and how will we run them?
[00:04:05] Priya Singh: We'll run three primary suites: 1) short-qa latency/throughput (p95 and p50), 2) accuracy evaluation on NyxAI's labeled set (we'll use the 500 sample queries they agreed to provide), 3) long-context summarization throughput and quality (ROUGE/semantic). For latency we'll measure single-request cold and warm (with KV cache primed) and also batched throughput at target concurrencies. We'll collect token/sec, GPU utilization, and per-token cost estimates.
[00:04:35] Dr. Lena Ortiz: How many GPUs or instance types are we assuming for each model?
[00:04:38] Priya Singh: For the POC bench we'll provision 1-2 A100s for the largest models (Falcon 40B / MPT-30B), and cheaper infer types (H100 or 80GB A10 alternatives) for 13B/7B quantized. We'll map each model to a recommended config in the benchmark report, with throughput and cost per 1M tokens.
[00:04:56] Marcus Chen: Ok. What about quantization and quality regressions — how do we handle that?
[00:04:59] Priya Singh: We'll test float16 baseline then 4-bit/QLoRA style quantizations where supported, and compare accuracy on the eval set. If quantization causes >5% drop on the key metric we recommend using a higher precision profile or different model. Redwood Optimize also suggests quantization profiles per workload.
[00:05:13] Aisha Bello: Any legal concerns about model weights or licenses?
[00:05:16] Jordan Mills: Good call — we'll note license checks. We avoid deploying models with incompatible licenses for customer data. We'll include a model-licensing note in the POC packet.
[00:05:24] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Timeline? we need to move quickly, ideally a 6 week runway to decision.
[00:05:28] Jordan Mills: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — share benchmark plan and sample queries; Week 1-2 — Redwood runs bench across shortlisted models; Week 3 — deliver bench report and recommendation; Week 4-6 — pilot on dedicated infra if we proceed. So 4-6 weeks total to decision/pilot.
[00:05:47] Priya Singh: For accuracy we need the labeled eval set; if you can provide the 500 queries and ground truth by Monday we'll start bench Tuesday.
[00:05:54] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We can deliver a CSV by Monday.
[00:05:58] Jordan Mills: Great. Any blockers?
[00:06:01] Marcus Chen: We need cost estimates upfront to sign off — hosted vs dedicated comparisons and commitment tiers.
[00:06:06] Jordan Mills: We'll include ballpark per-1M token pricing plus dedicated commit ranges in the proposal.
[00:06:10] Aisha Bello: We also want to run a small adversarial test — HX cases where model hallucinates. can you support evaluation on that?
[00:06:16] Priya Singh: Yes we'll add an adversarial holdout set and measure hallucination rate.
[00:06:20] Jordan Mills: Quick note on telemetry — we'll instrument traces and per-token cost metrics, and share a dashboard.
[00:06:26] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Great. Any immediate technical concerns from SE side?
[00:06:30] Marcus Chen: One: network egress for hosted runs. Two: SSO for our team. Three: ability to rotate keys regularly.
[00:06:36] Priya Singh: All doable. We'll surface SSO integration doc; KMS rotation supported, and egress can be minimized by obfuscating PII during bench.
[00:06:43] Jordan Mills: Okay let's run through the model tradeoffs one more time quickly.
[00:06:46] Priya Singh: Short bullets: Mistral 7B — great latency/cost, good instruction baseline. Llama-3 13B — strong in many QA tasks, good tradeoff when quantized. Falcon-40B — quality in some knowledge tasks but heavier and more expensive. MPT-30B — flexible but varies. Guanaco/OpenAssistant tuned 13B — best bet if we fine-tune/LoRA for domain. We'll pick 3 models to benchmark initially: Mistral 7B, Llama-3 13B (quant), and a tuned Guanaco 13B. Add Falcon40 as an optional run if license OK.
[00:07:13] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. For multilingual we want the Mistral and Llama comparisons prioritized.
[00:07:18] Jordan Mills: Next steps recap — Jordan to send POC packet and pricing; Priya to share benchmark template and schedule bench; NyxAI to send 500 sample queries and an adversarial set by Monday. Redwood to deliver bench report in 2 weeks.
[00:07:35] Marcus Chen: I'll also send our telemetry replay to simulate concurrency.
[00:07:39] Aisha Bello: And we'll review security docs.
[00:07:42] Jordan Mills: Perfect. Any final questions?
[00:07:44] Dr. Lena Ortiz: None here. Thanks.
[00:07:46] Jordan Mills: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the POC packet.
[00:07:50] [crosstalk] 
[00:08:10] Jordan Mills: (post meeting notes) we'll target bench start Tuesday pending CSV.
[00:08:18] (recording continues with some administrative chat and wrap up, timestamps skipped)
[00:15:00] Jordan Mills: end of main meeting — recording saved.
